text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Total posts a 50 percent rise in profits to 5.6 billion francs for 1996.
-- Electricity supplier EDF considers restructuring its accounting, seeks to increase capital to 55 billion francs from a current 2.6 billion, more in line with the company's value.
-- Credit Lyonnais U.S. branch considers setting up a joint venture with an American investment bank.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Unions at state-owned SNCF railway operator call strike against planned rail reform.
-- Bundesbank governor Hans Tietmeyer says a normalisation of the dollar/mark parity is reaching its end, sees the mark remaining a strong currency.
-- Canal Plus pay-TV channel and TF1 channel shares plunge at Paris bourse as analysts worry over the viability of their competing digital-TV bouquets in France.
L'AGEFI
-- Government may not be able to decide whether to privatise Thomson-CSF through private placement or public sale before February.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Hans Tietmeyer sees dollar rise near its end, remarks cause dollar to lose ground slightly against the mark.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis says GDP may rise more than the government forecast of 2.3 percent this year thanks to a favourable international situation and a strong dollar.
-- Danone food group chairman Franck Riboud says in an interview that Danone is reaping the benefits of its growth, operating margin is up for the first time in four years at 8.9 percent of turnover.
-- Social Security fund CNAM signs agreement with state on its commitment to financial health cost targets.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Accounts reshuffling at EDF may be a first step toward privatisation.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Appeals court rejects bid by TF1 to block Canal Plus merger with Nethold on grounds that it breached a previous agreement on sports broadcasts between Canal and TF1.
